subject: quokka
title: The World's Happiest Animal Has a Dark Way to Escape Predators

scenes.text: The world's happiest animal has a brutal escape plan.
The quokka is a small wallaby from Western Australia, famous for its smile in selfies.
A mother carries her joey in a pouch, and she controls the pouch muscles.
When a predator is closing in, she can relax them. The joey drops out.
It lies there writhing and hissing. The predator turns to the noise, and the mother gets away.
It isn't a throw, as the internet claims. But the logic is cold: she can have another.

description:
The quokka, the small Australian wallaby known as the world's happiest animal, has a harsh way of escaping predators.
According to conservation biologist Matthew Hayward of the University of Newcastle, Australia, macropods have strong control over their pouch muscles, and a fleeing mother with a larger joey can relax them so the joey falls out. The joey lies writhing and hissing on the ground, attracting the predator's attention while the mother escapes. Quokkas do not throw their babies, as viral posts claim, and kangaroos and other wallabies do the same thing. The mother is a proven breeder who can reproduce again, which is why the behaviour persists.
Does this change how you see that smile? Comment below.
